From:G.A.Matthews, ESSEX.

The Sony TV problem talked of in
the last Outlet is due to
'vertical blanking'. It isn't a
problem with video recorders or
most other gadgets that plug
into a scart socket. Computers
usually update every 50th of a
second. Sony TV's have a system
designed to give a steadier
picture. If it isn't exactly in
sync with the computer the TV
updates a split second before or
after the computer hence the
shaking picture. I have the
technical info sheet which
recommends opening the computer
or ideally the TV and soldering
a diode which slows the vertical
blanking to a speed that the
computer can handle.

PLEASE NOTE: ALL TV'S CONTAIN
HIGH VOLTAGES. EVEN DISCONNECTED
FROM THE MAINS, CAPACITORS CAN
STILL DISCHARGE.

I have a star LC10 printer, I
had problems when I bought it.
Possibly the shop may have
mucked around with the dip
switches. I think they had been
using it as a display model then
I realised that it was set up to
emulate an IBM proprinter, I got
the dip switches right but it is
not completely Epson. Epson
seems only to be a loose
standard, my Centronics GLP was
supposed to be Epson-compatible
but it was only partly so, the
Star is a very good printer but
not 100% Epson.

I think the handbook I got with
the Sam is the worst handbook
that I have ever seen. Come back
Sinclair, all is forgiven. Well
actually not - my Speccy is in
dire straits - held together
with sticky tape. I'm reluctant
to have it repaired. My experi-
ence last time was not good. I
took it to my local computer
shop and two weeks later I got
it back from them with a sticker
saying Verran on it, It did work
but not very well. I like the
Speccy but oh, how I wish Sir
Clive had made it a bit more
robust.
                 G.A. Matthews

From: Mr. E. Chipchase,ROTHERHAM

Dear Sir,

I have a +3 and Wordmaster with
Typeliner.  I find great enjoy-
ment doing a Newsletter for our
Social Club.  It certainly makes
a better format and, with the
graphics, has become a monthly
feature to look forward to.

I had no knowledge of Word
Processing and DTP until I
retired two years ago.  I now
find it takes up all my spare
time.  At the age of 65 years it
is good to take on new hobbies.
I use Tasword Masterfile for
data and Tasword Tascale for
financial records.

Without the above I should not
be able to take on the position
of Treasurer for the Retired
Members and I am also Secretary
and Treasurer of the National
P.S.V. Photographic Competition.

When I first started I had a 128
with two micro-drives but the +3
makes life easier.

Can anyone can tell me how or
where I can purchase a 3.5"
drive. Every local shop says
there's no way that they will
work on the +3, but in Outlet
No.38 Lief Mortensen says they
will. He even gives a program to
format one. A second drive would
complete my system.

Outlet is the one thing I can
make time for. It must be the
ultimate mag. for the Spectrum.

Thanks again for a most enter-
taining Magazine.

          E. Chipchase


To E. Chipchase from Brian Gaff

Yes, the reason most shops say
you cannot fit their drives is
because they usually need to be
opened up and the links moved to
make it appear as drive B. Also,
either an adaptor, or a new
cable will need fitting as most
drives come with a socket header
and not an edge connector on the
cable.

Most 3.5" drives will work, but
the cheapest I have found so far
are those made for the CPC range
by Phil Craven at around `80.
His address is 212 Dudley Hill
Road, Bradford, W. Yorks. (tel
0274 636652). In fact, any drive
for the CPC 6128, should run on
the +3.             Brian Gaff

To Reg Jeffs from Brian

Sorry, I've no time left to type
in your lengthy letter (remember
textfiles are much appreciated)
so must answer briefly...

If files'disappear' from the DIR
after swapping files in the SAM
directory using AUTOMENU (OUTLET
34) then just save one or two
dummy files until they appear.It
just means you swapped an unused
file position into the used area
of the directory instead of
swapping two files.The DIR stops
if it finds an unused directory
position (that is, completely
unused - not an ERASED section).
Generally, AVOID swapping files
with unused directory positions.

To get SAM to send control codes
to your printer use OPEN #3;"B"
first. Use CLOSE #3: OPEN #3;"P"
to get back to LLISTING etc.

Regarding OUTCLASS, I hope soon
to have a special one written
each month for the SAM version
of OUTLET.

Conversion of DIMSORTER to SAM
will be quite difficult and I do
not know when it can be done.
INSTAMATCHIT I have done and
hope to put in this issue (but I
would prefer further testing).
I have made a note of your other
requests for a BASIC search and
replace and a code to REMs
routine like our REMSTORE on the
Spectrum and also AUTOCHARS.
                        - Brian

From Simon Greenfield, LINCOLN



Dear Ron & Brian,

I'd just like to bring your and
other readers attention to an
excellent program for all
budding SAM/Star LC10C users

month's issue of Format magazine

is only a seven-colour printer.

colours to cater for this, but

Mr. Talbot gives a very speedy

PRICE: `3.95 (`4.95 if overseas)

From Dave Marriott, NOTTINGHAM

Dear Brian,

Thanks for your extensive reply
to my letter about problems with
large Sam BASIC programs in
Issue 40. What you say about
setting up the tables makes
sense but the main problem I was
having - RUN or CLEAR hanging up
completely - turned out to be
caused by an obscure ROM bug,for
which, after I wrote to you, I
managed to get a "semi-official"
fix. I was getting so frustrated
with it I rang Sam Computers
direct, and they referred me to
Andy Wright, no less. I sent him
a disc with the program and an
explanation, and he very quickly
found the solution.

Evidently it occurs when CLEAR
or RUN is setting up variables
for LABELS. If there are more
than 512 bytes' worth of these
(names plus values) then the
Variables area has to be
extended "in flight", and
thereafter the CLEAR/RUN hangs
up whilst trying to compile
PROC's or FN's.

Andy sent me a fix in the form
of a piece of code which is
loaded into the top part of the
Line Interrupt Colour Buffer
(presumably for want of anywhere
more convenient. More than 60 or
so colour changes on a screen
will overwrite the code) and is
patched in by altering the
"Command Vector" Sysvar to point

to it. It increases the initial
size of the Numeric Variables
area by 1000 bytes and, in my
case, solves the problem.

        Yours Sincerely,

          Dave Marriott


Thanks, Dave. The other various
points in your letter are noted
although I think it wise for
users to avoid using lots of
LABELS. I've never used them yet
because the procedures are so
excellently implemented on SAM I
can see no need (I trust this
problem doesn't also occur if
there should be more than just a
few procedures??!!).
                      - Brian C

From: W. E. Thomson, ALDEBURGH


A few points about SAM: points
(1)-(3) are "matters arising"
from previous OUTLETs; (4) is
new.

(1) Although usually I find that
the 1st character sent to the
printer after power-up is lost,
there is one program in which
this never happens. The printing
part is:

 OPEN #5,"B"
 PRINT #5,CHR$ 27;"M";<more
 control characters>
 LLIST L1-1 TO L2
 PRINT #5,<control characters>
 CLOSE #5

(2) The statement "FOR A=A TO.."
where A has previously been a
simple variable, leads to "A not
found"(unlike Spectrum). You can
get over this by introducing A
not by, say, "LET A=1" but by
"FOR A=1 TO 0: NEXT A".[No, use
LET B=A: FOR A=B TO  - BC]

(3) PRINT PEEK 15 gives the ROM
version number, without the
decimal point; e.g., version 3.0
leads to printing "30".

(4) If you use DUMP CHR$ in MODE
3, with its usual 85 characters
to a line, you will get a line
feed after the 80th character as
well as one after the 85th,
unless you have altered SVAR 14
from its usual value of 79 to,
say, 255.

Although SAM, like Spectrum, has
user-defined graphics,you cannot
enter them from the keyboard by
pressing a "graphics" key then
one of a set of keys. You could,
of course, assign suitable codes
by the"KEY posn,code" statement.
There are, however, 7 codes in
the range 144-168 that can be
produced by pressing SYMBOL+key.

These codes and the keys (in 2
cases a choice of keys) are:

 CODE   KEY       CODE     KEY

 148   O or S      151      V
 156     D         157      Y
 158     B         165   I or M
 168     C

These must be used within
strings;on power-up (or reset) a
space is produced, but POKE UDG
" "+n,m with SYMBOL+key produc-
ing the "space" between the
quotes, and n ranging from 0 to
7, with suitable values of m,
will assign a character to the
chosen SYMBOL+key, just like the
Spectrum's POKE USR "A".

                 - W.E. Thomson

Good tips! The last complements
a routine I was working on just
before I got your letter(honest)
called SHOWUDGS. It enables all
usual Spectrum UDGs from A to U
to be typed directly in strings
- but you need first to load and
call a procedure.     - Brian C

First, Hello to all Outlet mem-
bers and congrats to the editors
for the excellent job they do. I
hope the following information
may be of interest.

Whilst watching Dr. Andy Wright
demonstrating the new Masterdos,
I noticed that Andy was using an
exclamation mark(!)to modify the
DIR command.On querying this, it
was found the mod. worked with
the existing Samdos2. Normally,
if Device is D1, to obtain a
directory of drive 2 one enters
DIR 2 and gets a full directory.
If,however,you only need a short
directory then enter DIR 2! This
will give a short directory of
the non-current device.

The same syntax can be used with
a selective directory,regardless
of which device is current,e.g.,
DIR 1;"*.let"! will give a short
directory of the selected files.
Also, this may be used to direct
a DIR into a string, e.g...

     OPEN #4:
     RECORD TO A$:
     DIR #4;1!:
     RECORD STOP:
     CLOSE #4

     or...

     OPEN #4:
     RECORD TO A$:
     DIR #4;1"*.LETT"!:
     RECORD STOP:
     CLOSE #4

For those members who have not
used this facility,both the non-
selective and selective versions
give a full catalogue by ommitt-
ing the"!".Just change the drive
No. as required.NOTE,this method
does not recognise hidden files
(This facility is only a small
part of what this syntax will do
in the new MasterDos.I'm eagerly
waiting my copy).

Any member wishing to, may
contact me at the address at the
head of this letter. Best wishes
to all.            - David Hall

Many thanks David. I didn't know
a DIR! with a * was possible as
it's not in the manual! I tried
DIR 1!;"*.S" which doesn't work.
                     - Brian C.

From: Thurstan Felstead, RUISLIP

It's about time I wrote again,as
since my last missive there have
been a number of developments.

On 13/09/90 I received the new
ROM/DOS upgrade for my Coupe
from SAMCo. This was not before
time as I, like many others, had
been waiting literally months
for the upgrade. I bought my
Coupe in February of this year
from SRS Microsystems in Watford
with my primary use for the
machine to be program develop -
ment. However, due to the faults
in the ROM I decided it would be
best for my sanity to wait for
the new ROM version before
trying to get to grips with the
machine.

This has meant that my Coupe has
been sitting redundantly on my
desk for the past eight months.
I make no further comments,
except to say - paying `400 for
an elegantly styled bookrest is
not my idea of fun. With the new
ROM/DOS the machine is beginning
to live up to my expections, but
there are a couple of things
that I want to comment on. The
first is the display quality.
When I bought my Coupe, I also
invested in a new TV with a
SCART input as I was sick of the
poor quality picture from my old
14" colour portable. I also use
a Spectrum +3 extensively and
was pleased to find that I could
connect this machine to the
SCART TV as well.

The picture quality from the +3
is consistently excellent, with
sharp definition and bright
colours, however,the output from
the Coupe on SCART is a differ-
ent matter. The first noticeable
thing when comparing it to the
+3's output is the picture
brightness. When I switch from
TV to +3 I have to turn the
brightness and contrast controls
down because the picture is too
bright. When I switch from TV to
Coupe or from +3 to Coupe I find
I have to turn the brightness
and contrast up to get a visible
image. This difference in
brightness may be due to the
fact that the output from the +3
is TTL RGB and the output from
the Coupe is Linear RGB.

However, there's another matter,
a symptom that I describe as
picture "ghosting". This occurs
when a light and dark colour
meet, with a duplicate "ghost"
image appearing to the right of
the original. Fiddling with the
picture controls improves things
slightly, but does not cure the
problem. Funnily enough it is
not so noticeable when you are
using a Coupe on UHF (TV Aerial)
Output, although it is still
there. Considering that SCART is
a superior display standard then
something is definitely wrong.
In addition, an audible back -
ground hum can be heard from
the TV speaker when using the
Coupe on SCART, and I think that
this is also linked.

I wrote a letter to MGT in
February outlining the problem.
They wrote back in April saying
they thought my machine was
faulty and to return it to them.
Unfortunately they went into
receivership just as I was about
to arrange for the collection of
my machine. I have written to
the Receivers and SAMCo about it
but haven't received a reply.  I
do hope that the fault is due to
something being incorrectly
adjusted in the display circuit,
or can be solved by say,solder-
ing a resistor between two pins
somewhere, as it really does mar
the machine's performance. I
mean, what's the point of having
wonderful colourful graphics if
you can't make them out
properly.

So SAMCo,if you are listening...
You may remember (or not as the
case may be) my plea for help in
Outlet No. 33(May 1990) about my
faulty +3 printer port. On the
26th October you'll be pleased
to hear the problem was finally
solved when I fitted a new PCB
provided by VSE Technical Ser-
vices.The problem is my DMP-2160
is now functioning incorrectly,
the print quality is appalling.
I recently obtained CP/M Plus
for my +3 from Microsnips and am
investigating the possibility of
file transfer between this
machine and IBM PCs. The reason
is I have been using IBMs since
April, when I started at Brunel
University, Uxbridge as a Comp-
uter Operator in the Department
of Computer Science.

In my travels I have noticed a
number of IBM PC CP/M packages
available for the PC, including
an excellent public domain one
from the Lancaster University's
PD Soft library called 'Z80MU'
which is a Z80 microprocessor
and CP/M 2.2 emulation package.
Since one reason for having a
standard operating system such
as CP/M is to allow portability
between machines, file transfer
between two machines running
under the same O/S should be
easier to accomplish than if
they aren't. eg. converting a
file from a +3 running under
CP/M to an IBM PC running under
CP/M should be easier than
converting from a +3 running
under +3DOS to an IBM PC running
under PC/MS DOS.

So, when using CP/M, the only
real problem we should encounter
is disk size and format.

Assuming all versions of CP/M
use the same format method, then
all we need to get right is the
size of the floppy drive used by
both machines. In this case the
easiest thing to do is get a
3.5" drive for the +3, as who
wants to attempt to get a 3"
running on an IBM PC! Anyway, a
drive that appears to fit our
requirements is the MGT Lifetime
Drive (now apparently being
produced by E.E.C. and not MGT).
I have not yet obtained a
Lifetime Drive, so at the moment
the above is still just a
theory.

However, major problems aside, I
will try to get the transfer up
and running by the beginning of
next year (If I can get the
Lifetime Drive). I'll keep you
posted.


I think I have finally solved
that great mystery of the
Universe - what CP/M really
stands for. According to my
exhaustive research it stands
for 'Control Processor/ Micro-
computer'. This may be right,
who knows, probably not even
Digital Research! It is good to
see that a number of SAM PD
publishers have recently sprung
up. The ones I know about are:

His catalogue currently has the

On a final note, a quick plug
for my first commercially
published game 'The Boxer '
which has just been released on

C64 formats.

I was responsible for the game
design and Spectrum coding. The
Amstrad version recently got a
review in Amstrad Action with an
overall rating of 67% and was
described as "Certainly one of
the better management games".

Continue to keep up the good
work both of you.

       Thurstan Felstead.

To T. Felstead from Brian Gaff

The picture quality problem you
mention has cropped up before,
and is due to an effect called
ringing. This occurs when the
terminating impedance is not
within the design specs. In
other words, it could be that
Bruce had a different monitor to
yours, when he designed it!

Standards like SCART are rather
lax, and its only when items get
into the real world that these
problems show up. I would
suggest you have a word with
Paul Thomas of PBT Electoronics,
as he assured me the ghosting
effect was curable in most
cases.

Paul is the person who would
have looked at your SAM at MGT
anyway, and he now handles all
the machines returned under
warranty. Their address is Unit
17 Port Talbot Workshops,
Addison Road, Port Talbot, West
Glamorgan SA12 6HZ (Tel: 0639
885008).

There are a lot of different
interpretations of what CP/M
means, I prefer Control
Program/Monitor. I have not
investigated the concept of
reading CP/M discs with a PC, as
my machine only has a 5.25"
drive anyway. However, it is
perfectly possible to transfer
files across the RS232.

There is a PD Spectrum program
that allows Xmodem over the
serial link, though it operates
undef +3DOS, not CP/M. You could
try getting MEX to do it though.

Another program that might be
useful, is DU49.COM. This has
the ability to format discs to
many non-Amstrad formats, that
your PC CP/M emulator might
manage to read. It also
configures the host machine to
read these other formats.

I would be tempted, in your
position, to get a cheap stand-
alone PC second drive, as these
seem to stand a good chance of
working on the +3 without any
alterations. DU49.COM can format

3.5" discs to high capacities,
with the added advantage that
+3DOS is quite happy to read and
write to them.

                  Brian G.

From: Donald Pemberton


Dear Ron & Brian,

It was disconcerting, to put it
mildly, to learn that the +3 has
been discontinued. Sudden panic!
What am I to do if my +3 breaks
down with some irreparable
complaint? How shall I be able
to access all the data I have in
my Masterfile files, my Tascalc
spreadsheet records and all the
correspondence and notes saved
on Tasword+3, not forgetting my
14 Outlet disks?

Could I run these 3 inch disks
on a Spectrum "B" Drive attached
to a Spectrum 2A?

My present set-up is a +3 with
multiface3 and a M-1009 printer
plus a 48K Spectrum+ with 2
microdrives.

Is a +D Drive incorporating the
Megamat DOS in Outlet 39 a
feasible alternative?

Your advice would be greatly
appreciated.

        Donald Pemberton

To D. Pemberton from Brian Gaff


Unfortunately, you cannot just
plug a drive onto the +2A.
Though the ROM is all there, the
disc control circuitry is not!
If you read the manual for the
2A, it says that you will need
an SI-1 interface, and a DD-1
drive to make it work.

The bad news is that Amstrad do
not make the interface, and the
DD-1 has been discontinued!
However, I am assured that
spares for the +3, including
disc drives, are plentiful,
though I guess you may have to
spend some time finding a
repairer willing to fix it.

I think you may be getting a
little confused about drives.
The +D is an interface which can
use almost any drive you care to
attach to it - assuming it has
its own PSU of course. Megamat
is purely a +3DOS program, which
is used on that machine, with a
3.5" drive attached to the B
drive port. The +D cannot read
+3 discs directly.

                    Brian G.

From:P.D. Bell, SHOREHAM BY SEA

I may be of help to Derek Morgan
with his printing problem.

I suspect that his DUMP from SAM
looks like a fair imitation of a
Venetian blind, even though he

methods of preventing unwanted
line feeds. I suggest that his

overy printer cable, about 2"
below its own connector, making
sure it was the right way up,
with the arrow on top, and the
red edge wire at that end of the
connector.

It can be closed  using  pliers,
but far better to use a vice.
The resulting cable can be
swapped between Opus and SAM,
and when in the latter position,
will cure the DUMP problem but
don't ask me why!

I spent ages checking the
continuity and positions of the
individual wires to no avail.
MGT said my dip switches must be
in the wrong position, which was
one of the first things I had
checked at the start. At the
time I was so cheesed off with
the problems SAM had, I nearly
threw it back.

By the way, the transformers of
some printers are subject to
overheating and failure as they
are cut to the bone for profit.
This from a repair engineer. I
have drilled holes in the casing
of mine, near the offending
beast which cost an arm and a
leg to replace. A case of air
today or gone tomorrow.

Will Tasman ever come up with an
equivalent of Tasword+2 or 3 for
SAM? With the memory available,
Seven Stars could join in with
umpteen fonts on call with QUAL-
ITAS and the excellent routine
for designing one's own fonts,
not restricted to 8x8 format.

            Regards,

           Peter Bell






Many thanks, Peter   - Brian C.

Dear Brian,

Thanks for your extensive reply to my letter about problems with large Sam BASIC programs in Issue 40. What you say about setting up the tables makes sense but the main problem I was having - RUN or CLEAR hanging up completely - turned out to be caused by an obscure ROM bug,for which, after I wrote to you, I managed to get a "semi-official" fix. I was getting so frustrated with it I rang Sam Computers direct, and they referred me to Andy Wright, no less. I sent him a disc with the program and an explanation, and he very quickly found the solution.

Evidently it occurs when CLEAR or RUN is setting up variables for LABELS. If there are more than 512 bytes' worth of these (names plus values) then the Variables area has to be extended "in flight", and thereafter the CLEAR/RUN hangs up whilst trying to compile PROC's or FN's.

Andy sent me a fix in the form of a piece of code which is loaded into the top part of the Line Interrupt Colour Buffer (presumably for want of anywhere more convenient. More than 60 or so colour changes on a screen will overwrite the code) and is patched in by altering the "Command Vector" Sysvar to point

to it. It increases the initial size of the Numeric Variables area by 1000 bytes and, in my case, solves the problem.

Yours Sincerely,

Dave Marriott

A few points about SAM: points (1)-(3) are "matters arising" from previous OUTLETs; (4) is new.

(1) Although usually I find that the 1st character sent to the printer after power-up is lost, there is one program in which this never happens. The printing part is:

OPEN #5,"B" PRINT #5,CHR$ 27;"M";<more control characters> LLIST L1-1 TO L2 PRINT #5,<control characters> CLOSE #5

(2) The statement "FOR A=A TO.." where A has previously been a simple variable, leads to "A not found"(unlike Spectrum). You can get over this by introducing A not by, say, "LET A=1" but by "FOR A=1 TO 0: NEXT A".[No, use LET B=A: FOR A=B TO  - BC]

(3) PRINT PEEK 15 gives the ROM version number, without the decimal point; e.g., version 3.0 leads to printing "30".

(4) If you use DUMP CHR$ in MODE 3, with its usual 85 characters to a line, you will get a line feed after the 80th character as well as one after the 85th, unless you have altered SVAR 14 from its usual value of 79 to, say, 255.

Although SAM, like Spectrum, has user-defined graphics,you cannot enter them from the keyboard by pressing a "graphics" key then one of a set of keys. You could, of course, assign suitable codes by the"KEY posn,code" statement. There are, however, 7 codes in the range 144-168 that can be produced by pressing SYMBOL+key.

These codes and the keys (in 2 cases a choice of keys) are:

CODE   KEY       CODE     KEY

148   O or S      151      V

```text
 156     D         157      Y
 158     B         165   I or M
 168     C
```

These must be used within strings;on power-up (or reset) a space is produced, but POKE UDG " "+n,m with SYMBOL+key produc- ing the "space" between the quotes, and n ranging from 0 to 7, with suitable values of m, will assign a character to the chosen SYMBOL+key, just like the Spectrum's POKE USR "A".

- W.E. Thomson

DAVID HALL 77, NEWTON ROAD, STOWMARKET,SUFFOLK.IP14 5AE First, Hello to all Outlet mem- bers and congrats to the editors for the excellent job they do. I hope the following information may be of interest.

Whilst watching Dr. Andy Wright demonstrating the new Masterdos, I noticed that Andy was using an exclamation mark(!)to modify the DIR command.On querying this, it was found the mod. worked with the existing Samdos2. From: Thurstan Felstead, RUISLIP

It's about time I wrote again,as since my last missive there have been a number of developments.

On 13/09/90 I received the new ROM/DOS upgrade for my Coupe from SAMCo. This was not before time as I, like many others, had been waiting literally months for the upgrade. I bought my Coupe in February of this year from SRS Microsystems in Watford with my primary use for the machine to be program develop - ment. However, due to the faults in the ROM I decided it would be best for my sanity to wait for the new ROM version before trying to get to grips with the machine.

This has meant that my Coupe has been sitting redundantly on my desk for the past eight months. I make no further comments, except to say - paying `400 for an elegantly styled bookrest is not my idea of fun. With the new ROM/DOS the machine is beginning to live up to my expections, but there are a couple of things that I want to comment on. The first is the display quality. When I bought my Coupe, I also invested in a new TV with a SCART input as I was sick of the poor quality picture from my old 14" colour portable. I also use a Spectrum +3 extensively and was pleased to find that I could connect this machine to the SCART TV as well.

The picture quality from the +3 is consistently excellent, with sharp definition and bright colours, however,the output from the Coupe on SCART is a differ- ent matter. The first noticeable thing when comparing it to the +3's output is the picture brightness. When I switch from TV to +3 I have to turn the brightness and contrast controls down because the picture is too bright. When I switch from TV to Coupe or from +3 to Coupe I find I have to turn the brightness and contrast up to get a visible image. This difference in brightness may be due to the fact that the output from the +3 is TTL RGB and the output from the Coupe is Linear RGB.

However, there's another matter, a symptom that I describe as picture "ghosting". This occurs when a light and dark colour meet, with a duplicate "ghost" image appearing to the right of the original. Fiddling with the picture controls improves things slightly, but does not cure the problem. Funnily enough it is not so noticeable when you are using a Coupe on UHF (TV Aerial) Output, although it is still there. Considering that SCART is a superior display standard then something is definitely wrong. In addition, an audible back - ground hum can be heard from the TV speaker when using the Coupe on SCART, and I think that this is also linked.

I wrote a letter to MGT in February outlining the problem. They wrote back in April saying they thought my machine was faulty and to return it to them. Unfortunately they went into receivership just as I was about to arrange for the collection of my machine. I have written to the Receivers and SAMCo about it but haven't received a reply.  I do hope that the fault is due to something being incorrectly adjusted in the display circuit, or can be solved by say,solder- ing a resistor between two pins somewhere, as it really does mar the machine's performance. I mean, what's the point of having wonderful colourful graphics if you can't make them out properly.

So SAMCo,if you are listening... You may remember (or not as the case may be) my plea for help in Outlet No. 33(May 1990) about my faulty +3 printer port. On the 26th October you'll be pleased to hear the problem was finally solved when I fitted a new PCB provided by VSE Technical Ser- vices.The problem is my DMP-2160 is now functioning incorrectly, the print quality is appalling. I recently obtained CP/M Plus for my +3 from Microsnips and am investigating the possibility of file transfer between this machine and IBM PCs. The reason is I have been using IBMs since April, when I started at Brunel University, Uxbridge as a Comp- uter Operator in the Department of Computer Science.

In my travels I have noticed a number of IBM PC CP/M packages available for the PC, including an excellent public domain one from the Lancaster University's PD Soft library called 'Z80MU' which is a Z80 microprocessor and CP/M 2.2 emulation package. Since one reason for having a standard operating system such as CP/M is to allow portability between machines, file transfer between two machines running under the same O/S should be easier to accomplish than if they aren't. eg. converting a file from a +3 running under CP/M to an IBM PC running under CP/M should be easier than converting from a +3 running under +3DOS to an IBM PC running under PC/MS DOS.

So, when using CP/M, the only real problem we should encounter is disk size and format.

Assuming all versions of CP/M use the same format method, then all we need to get right is the size of the floppy drive used by both machines. In this case the easiest thing to do is get a 3.5" drive for the +3, as who wants to attempt to get a 3" running on an IBM PC! Anyway, a drive that appears to fit our requirements is the MGT Lifetime Drive (now apparently being produced by E.E.C. and not MGT). I have not yet obtained a Lifetime Drive, so at the moment the above is still just a theory.

However, major problems aside, I will try to get the transfer up and running by the beginning of next year (If I can get the Lifetime Drive). I'll keep you posted.

I think I have finally solved that great mystery of the Universe - what CP/M really stands for. According to my exhaustive research it stands for 'Control Processor/ Micro- computer'. This may be right, who knows, probably not even Digital Research! It is good to see that a number of SAM PD publishers have recently sprung up. The ones I know about are:

CONTACT, 10 Ricardo Road, Old Windsor, Berks., SL4 2NU.

FASTLINE, 1 Ryelands Place, 0UX. Turbo, 8 Healey, Lakeside, Tamworth, Staffs., B77 2RF. CMS

SAM Coupe PD, 70 Donald Drive, Chadwell Heath, Romford, Essex, RM6 6DU.

A special mention goes to:

Guy Middleton,35,Victoria Mount Horsforth, LEEDs, LS18 4PU. He produces SAM graphics demos and sells them at a very reasonable `1.50 each, eventually putting them into the Public Domain as Freeware.

His catalogue currently has the excellent Total Recall Movie Trailer Demo (256K and 512K versions, please specify when ordering) and the Robocop Demo (one version for both 256K and 512K machines).  At the moment you can only get the Robocop Demo from him, as it doesn't become Freeware until December 1st 1990.  Also for December 1st he promises a Star Wars Demo and a Christmas Quiz with prizes.

On a final note, a quick plug for my first commercially published game 'The Boxer ' which has just been released on D&H Games' Cult budget label at `2.99 on Spectrum, Amstrad and C64 formats.

I was responsible for the game design and Spectrum coding. The Amstrad version recently got a review in Amstrad Action with an overall rating of 67% and was described as "Certainly one of the better management games".

Continue to keep up the good work both of you.

Yours sincerely,

Thurstan Felstead.

To T. Felstead from Brian Gaff

The picture quality problem you mention has cropped up before, and is due to an effect called ringing. This occurs when the terminating impedance is not within the design specs. In other words, it could be that Bruce had a different monitor to yours, when he designed it!

Standards like SCART are rather lax, and its only when items get into the real world that these problems show up. I would suggest you have a word with Paul Thomas of PBT Electoronics, as he assured me the ghosting effect was curable in most cases.

Paul is the person who would have looked at your SAM at MGT anyway, and he now handles all the machines returned under warranty. Their address is Unit 17 Port Talbot Workshops, Addison Road, Port Talbot, West Glamorgan SA12 6HZ (Tel: 0639 885008).

There are a lot of different interpretations of what CP/M means, I prefer Control Program/Monitor. I have not investigated the concept of reading CP/M discs with a PC, as my machine only has a 5.25" drive anyway. However, it is perfectly possible to transfer files across the RS232.

There is a PD Spectrum program that allows Xmodem over the serial link, though it operates undef +3DOS, not CP/M. You could try getting MEX to do it though.

Another program that might be useful, is DU49.COM. This has the ability to format discs to many non-Amstrad formats, that your PC CP/M emulator might manage to read. It also configures the host machine to read these other formats.

I would be tempted, in your position, to get a cheap stand- alone PC second drive, as these seem to stand a good chance of working on the +3 without any alterations. DU49.COM can format

3.5" discs to high capacities, with the added advantage that +3DOS is quite happy to read and write to them.

I think you may be getting a little confused about drives. The +D is an interface which can use almost any drive you care to attach to it - assuming it has its own PSU of course.
